chain.note: Both plans follow the paper's route: two network-based tape procedures, then the ring convolution, resampling and chirp, then assembly and costs. A establishes the saving for both networks: s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b<W_b m (S5.4), s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c<W_c m with the phase-kernel mechanism (S5.5), and s_b/W_b<m^tau and s_c/W_c<m^sigma with tau=sigma=1-2^{-50} (S5.6). A then feeds both into the interchange recurrence (S5.9) and the layer recurrence (S5.11.6). B derives the saving and tau only for the bit network (K3). For the butterfly layer it uses s/W<=m^sigma (S3.3.e) without ever establishing s_c<W_c m or s_c/W_c<m^sigma. It also lacks the P_M conjugation that turns edge kernels into slot calls, so its chain for the second procedure thins out.

errors.says: Method: the two bottlenecks (address interchange and butterfly layers) are sped up 'by one rank-saving linear network'.
errors.paper: Each procedure arises from its own fixed linear network; the layer uses the complex network's constants, which need not equal those of the chunk-swap (bit) network.

overall.reason: A carries the complex network's saving and its mechanism, which B lacks: weight additivity mod 4, odd weight giving translation kernels, the 27-coordinate C^{-1} repair, s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c, both exact deficits eta_b and eta_c, and s_c/W_c<m^sigma. A also carries the P_M basis change behind the phase-frame recursion and the full guard-constant derivation (C_0, C_1, total below C_0 d^{C_1}). B's advantages are minor details (the full exponent list, the per-row powers of p, the two-bit XOR, the 2n output length). B has one minor misstatement (one network for both procedures), and no item favours B.
